review.summary: SWE-agent’s central contribution is a purpose-designed agent-computer interface for repository-level software engineering, with tools and feedback tailored to language-model interaction. On SWE-bench, the reported results and interface ablations provide substantial evidence that interaction design—not only model choice—affects issue resolution, though evidence is limited to two large closed models and a specific benchmark/setup.

observations.claim: The paper reports meaningful benchmark performance, clearly evaluated against interactive and retrieval-based baselines.
Ablations support the claim that the editor and linting contribute to performance, rather than attributing all gains to the model alone.
The empirical scope is narrow: the reported evaluations and ablations rely on two leading models, with other models described as subpar rather than characterized in comparable detail.
observations.quote: All results, ablations, and analysis are based on two leading LMs

observations.claim: The design choices were partly informed by a small, hand-picked development set, leaving open how robustly the selected interface generalizes beyond those choices and benchmark conditions.
observations.quote: small set of hand-picked easier examples from the development split of SWE-bench

unresolved_questions: How well do the ACI’s gains transfer to other model families, repositories, and software-engineering task distributions?
Would the reported performance and ablation patterns persist under independent replications or different benchmark evaluation conditions?

I inspected the introduction, method, setup, main result, and part of the interface analysis; I did not inspect the full behavior analysis, conclusion, appendices, or every experiment, so broader limitations and operational details remain uncertain.
